title: Short Rib Ragu Pappardelle
summary: Slow-braised short rib ragu tossed through wide ribbons of pasta; rich winter comfort.
difficulty_reason: Simple steps, but it needs a good sear, a long braise and finishing the pasta in the sauce.

ingredients.line: 2.5 to 3 lb bone-in beef short ribs (1.2 to 1.5 kg)
1 1/4 cups (300 ml) red wine, such as cabernet sauvignon
1 parmesan rind, plus finely grated parmesan to finish

steps: Heat the oven to 285°F. Season the short ribs with salt and pepper, then sear in olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat until deeply browned on all sides. Set aside, leaving the fat in the pot.
Lower the heat to medium and soften the onion, carrot, celery and garlic for 3 to 4 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the red wine and simmer 5 to 6 minutes to cook off the alcohol, then add the chopped tomatoes.
Return the short ribs to the pot, cover with the beef stock, and tuck in the thyme, rosemary, bay leaves and parmesan rind.
Cover and braise in the oven for 4 hours, until the meat falls off the bone.
Lift the ribs out, discard the bones, and shred the meat on a tray. Fish the herbs and parmesan rind out of the sauce.
Return the shredded beef to the pot and simmer for 10 minutes to bring it together.
Meanwhile, boil the pappardelle for 2 minutes less than the package says.
Add the pasta to a pan over medium-low heat with a few ladles of ragu, and toss with splashes of pasta water and parmesan until silky.
Plate the pasta, spoon over more ragu, and finish with parmesan and parsley.
tips: Get a deep brown sear on the ribs; it builds most of the flavor.
Finish the pasta in the sauce with pasta water and parmesan for a silky coating.
The ragu keeps well and is even better the next day.
